alex: Ran a KV/prompt-cache profiling pass after yesterday's kernel selector rollout — hit rates tanked on tail workloads, and we saw a few GPU OOM spikes. Posting quick summary and samples.

alex: PROFILE SNAPSHOT (aggregate):
```
before: global_hit=0.62 per_prefix=0.74
after:  global_hit=0.41 per_prefix=0.53
median_lat_p95: +28ms
gpu_mem_delta: +18%
OOM_events: 7 spikes between 03:17-03:40 UTC
```

alex: Sampled keys show a ton of near-duplicates with tiny ephemeral suffixes (session nonces / timestamps). Looks like cache key entropy jumped after we started including routing/kernel path metadata.

maya: Wait — I thought key fingerprinting was unchanged. Did the kernel selector change mutate the key format? :thinking_face:

alex: It did. To support route-aware fallback we appended a kernel_id fragment to the cache key inside the runtime. That made keys unique across what used to be identical prompts. We didn't canonicalize ephemeral parts.

cheng: That's consistent with the hit drop. Essentially the key space exploded for long-running sessions and conversational prompts that append tokens like `#sess_12345`. Two quick mitigation ideas:
- canonicalize known ephemeral patterns (strip session ids, timestamps)
- add stable hashing that normalizes whitespace + unicode normalization before fingerprinting

cheng: Example canonicalizer (rough):
```
// pseudocode
k = normalize_unicode(k)
k = collapse_whitespace(k)
k = re.sub(r"sess_[0-9a-f]{6,}", "<SESS>", k)
key = sha1(k + model_shard_no_kernel)
```

leah: Also seeing the eviction/TTL config exacerbated this — with more unique keys the cold cache grew and our LRU churned hot prefixes out faster. On some hosts we set TTL=24h which now keeps a bunch of nearly-unused unique keys in RAM. We should ramp TTL based on observed reuse.

leah: Suggestion: short TTL for cold prefixes (5-15m), progressive ramp for prefixes with hit_rate > 0.6 up to hours. Also GC idle prefixes earlier when free_slabs < 20%.

simon: We should also consider slab fragmentation on GPU allocator. I profiled one of the OOM hosts and free_bytes looked healthy but allocation requests failed due to fragmentation/coalescing limits. The increased number of small objects (one per unique prompt) makes fragmentation worse.

alex: infra-bot posted an alert earlier:
```
[infra-bot] ALERT: gpu-rt-7 OOM spike series @ 2026-02-11T03:19Z. 7 events in 23m. Links: https://console/redwood/alerts/1234
```

maya: Proposed rollout plan to avoid regression: 
1) Revert kernel_id append in prod routing (quick rollback) to stop key explosion.
2) Deploy canonicalization + stable hashing patch behind a feature flag.
3) Canary TTL-ramp changes on 5% of hosts with traffic sampling.
4) Run slab/alloc tuning (reduce small-slab size, enable coalescing heuristics) on canary cluster.

alex: I'll create a small canary job and a dashboard with per-prefix hit-rate histogram + key-entropy metric. We need to track: global_hit, per_prefix_hit, unique_keys_per_min, slab_frag_pct, alloc_failures.

cheng: I'll own the canonicalization PR. I'll include a conservative regex list first (session IDs, ISO timestamps, request-ids) and opt-in transformation rules per model since some models rely on intact whitespace.

simon: I'll run allocator flamegraph on the canary nodes and try a change that coalesces adjacent small slabs. If that reduces fragmentation/OOM, we push to wider fleet.

leah: I'll implement TTL ramp config and a chaos test that simulates bursty long-tail prompts to validate there is no regression in latency.

maya: TL;DR: revert kernel-id key change in prod -> canary canonicalizer + TTL ramp + slab tuning -> monitor 24-48h -> roll forward. I'll update incident board and add owners. :white_check_mark:

alex: Thanks all. Will post PR links + canary dashboard once created.

maya: ping @cheng @simon @leah once you have PRs so we can coordinate the canary window.

alex: noted.

(reacts: alex :eyes:, maya :white_check_mark:)
